**Exclude installed dependencies from the scan.** When a contributor installs dependencies in the template server directory, this traversal enters `node_modules`. `@anthropic-ai/sdk@0.65.0` contains model IDs that match the test pattern, so the test can fail even when the template is correct.
Suggested fix
```diff --- "a/packages/create/tests/template-model-ids.test.ts" +++ "b/packages/create/tests/template-model-ids.test.ts" @@ -10,10 +10,11 @@ // hard-codes one generates a project whose AI chat fails at the first request. const RETIRED_CLAUDE_MODEL = /claude-3(?:-5|-7)?-(?:opus|sonnet|haiku)/ function listFiles(dir: string): Array { return readdirSync(dir).flatMap((entry) => { + if (entry === 'node_modules') return [] const full = join(dir, entry) return statSync(full).isDirectory() ? listFiles(full) : [full] }) } ```

Thanks for catching this. The scanner now ignores installed dependencies and still checks authored templates.

> AI review notes:
> Added a fixture containing both an SDK declaration with an old model ID and an authored template with the same ID. The authored file is detected, then the check passes after its model is updated. The original template model also fails the scanner negative control.
> The factory generated the Solid chat app outside the monorepo, built its client and SSR output, and built and type-checked the backend. A network-disconnected local mock verified the Haiku 4.5 request and streamed response. No provider request was made.

** Minor** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Flush the success marker before shutdown.** On POSIX, `execFile` captures stdout through a pipe. `manager.stop()` then calls `process.exit(0)`, which can discard the pending `console.log` write. The parent test can fail after both edits succeed. Write the marker with `process.stdout.write` and await its callback before calling `manager.stop()`. ([nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/api/process.html?utm_source=openai))
